mainTopic: צאן ברזל, ownership and בכורה; and whether taking interest from a גוי is proper
overview: The משנה rules that a צאן ברזל deal, where the receiver guarantees the animals' value, is forbidden between Jews because it is רבית, but allowed with a גוי. It also allows borrowing and lending with interest with a גוי or a גר תושב. The גמרא asks how this fits a משנה in בכורות, which seems to treat such animals as still belonging to the גוי. אביי answers that the two cases differ in who carries the risk, but רבא rejects that answer with two objections. רבא then explains that in both cases the receiver owns the animals. The offspring are exempt from בכורה only because the גוי can seize them, which puts a 'גוי's hand in the middle'. The גמרא then turns to the פסוק in משלי about interest money ending up with a king like שבור מלכא, and רב נחמן teaches that this applies even to interest from a גוי. רבא challenges him from the פסוק 'לנכרי תשיך' and then from our משנה. רב חייא בריה דרב הונא begins an answer that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The משנה forbids an iron-sheep deal between Jews
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that one may not take צאן ברזל from a Jew because it is רבית, but one may take it from גוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: You may not take 'iron sheep' from a Jew, because that is interest. But you may take 'iron sheep' from non-Jews.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens with a rule. A צאן ברזל deal between two Jews is forbidden as רבית, but it is allowed with a גוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a צאן ברזל deal, the receiver promises to always return the full value of the animals, no matter what happens. He also shares the profits with the owner. Since the owner's money is guaranteed, it works like a loan, and the extra profit he gets is interest. With a גוי there is no איסור רבית, so the deal is fine.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'iron sheep': an investment whose value is guaranteed, like iron that does not wear away
Interest, which is forbidden between Jews
One may accept (take on the deal)

steps.confusionAlert: צאן ברזל is not about real iron. 'Iron' means the owner's value is locked in and always comes back to him.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is the foundation for the גמרא's question. Calling it רבית treats the deal as a loan, which means the receiver is treated as owning the animals.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One may not accept 'iron sheep' from a Jew
phrases.notes: The receiver guarantees the full value of the animals and splits the profits with the owner.

phrases.english: because it is interest.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מְקַבְּלִין צֹאן בַּרְזֶל מִן הַגּוֹיִם,
phrases.english: But one may accept 'iron sheep' from non-Jews,

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A צאן ברזל deal is forbidden between Jews as רבית, but permitted with גוים.

steps.title: Lending with interest to non-Jews and a גר תושב
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds that one may borrow from and lend to גוים with interest, and the same applies to a גר תושב.
steps.simpleTranslation: You may borrow from them and lend to them with interest. The same is true of a גר תושב.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues. It is not only צאן ברזל: plain loans with interest are also allowed with a גוי and with a גר תושב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The איסור רבית applies only between Jews. A גר תושב keeps the seven Noahide מצוות but is not Jewish, so he is treated like a גוי for interest.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jewish resident who keeps the seven Noahide מצוות

phrases.english: and one may borrow from them and lend to them with interest.
And the same is true of a ger toshav.
phrases.notes: He keeps the seven Noahide laws but has not converted, so he is not Jewish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the permission with גוים from צאן ברזל to ordinary loans, and to a גר תושב
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Borrowing and lending with interest is allowed with גוים and with a גר תושב.

steps.title: A Jew lending a non-Jew's money
steps.stepSummary: A Jew may lend a גוי's money to another Jew with interest if it is done with the גוי's knowledge, but not if it is done with the Jew's knowledge.
steps.simpleTranslation: A Jew may lend out a non-Jew's money with the non-Jew's knowledge, but not with the Jew's knowledge.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a case of a Jewish middleman lending a גוי's money. Whether it is allowed depends on whose 'knowledge' the deal runs on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the deal is really the גוי's own loan, the interest belongs to him, so it is allowed. If it runs on the Jewish middleman's say, it looks like his loan, so it is forbidden. The גמרא will explain this line later.

phrases.english: A Jew may lend a non-Jew's money
with the knowledge of the non-Jew,
but not with the knowledge of the Jew.
phrases.notes: This is the Jewish middleman. The גמרא will explain this line later.

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה has three rules: no צאן ברזל between Jews; interest is fine with a גוי or גר תושב; a middleman may lend a גוי's money only 'with the גוי's knowledge.'
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a case of a Jewish middleman for a גוי's money
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Jew may lend a גוי's money with the גוי's knowledge, but not with the Jew's knowledge.

steps.title: Who owns the iron sheep? A contradiction from בכורות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the משנה means the animals belong to the receiver. It then brings a contradicting משנה, which says the offspring of צאן ברזל taken from גוים are exempt from בכורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean the animals are in the receiver's ownership? But there is a contradiction: if someone takes iron sheep from non-Jews, the babies are exempt from the firstborn rules!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points to a clash between our משנה and a משנה in בכורות about who owns צאן ברזל animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling the deal רבית treats it as a loan, so the Jewish receiver would own the animals. But the משנה in בכורות exempts the newborns from בכורה, and that only makes sense if the animals still belong to the גוי. So one משנה says the receiver owns them, and the other says the owner does.

keyTerms.meaning: And contradict them: a clash between two sources is raised
The holiness of a firstborn animal

steps.confusionAlert: The בכורה exemption is the proof of ownership. A firstborn is holy only if a Jew owns the mother, so 'exempt' means the גוי still owns it.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Is this to say that it stands in the ownership of the receiver?
But a contradiction is raised:
One who accepts iron sheep from non-Jews,
the offspring are exempt from the firstborn rules!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an ownership conclusion from the משנה's רבית ruling and challenges it
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication of step 1 that צאן ברזל is owned by the receiver
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה in בכורות exempts the offspring from בכורה, which shows that the גוי owner still owns the animals. That contradicts our משנה, which treats the receiver as owner.

steps.title: אביי: it depends on who carries the risk
steps.stepSummary: אביי resolves the contradiction. In בכורות the owner took on the risk of accident and price drop, so the animals are still his. In our משנה he did not, so they belong to the receiver.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: No problem. That case is where he takes on accidents and price drops. This case is where he did not take on accidents and price drops.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the contradiction. He says the two sources are talking about two differently arranged deals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ownership follows risk. If the original owner (the גוי in בכורות) takes on losses from accidents and falling prices, the animals stay his, so the newborns are exempt. In our משנה the receiver carries all the risk, so the animals count as his, and the owner's guaranteed profit is רבית.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult: there is no contradiction
This case ... that case: splitting two sources into different situations

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, whoever carries the risk of accident and price drop is treated as the owner. Watch out: רבא rejects this answer in steps 6 and 7 and gives his own in step 8.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the first attempt to resolve the contradiction. רבא's two objections that follow (steps 6 and 7) are aimed at exactly this risk-based distinction.

phrases.english: Abaye said: It is not difficult.
That case is where he accepts upon himself accidents and price drops,
phrases.notes: This is the בכורות case: there the גוי owner takes on the risk, so the animals stay his.

phrases.aramaic: הָא דְּלָא קַבֵּיל עֲלֵיהּ אוּנְסָא וְזוֹלָא.
phrases.english: this case is where he did not accept upon himself accidents and price drops.
phrases.notes: This is our משנה: the owner takes no risk, so the animals belong to the receiver.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each source refers to a different arrangement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources seemed to describe the same צאן ברזל deal, so they appeared to clash over ownership.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to אביי, ownership follows the risk. If the owner bears accident and price drop, he still owns the animals. If not, the receiver owns them. רבא later rejects this.

steps.title: If the owner carries the risk, it is not צאן ברזל
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges אביי: an arrangement where the owner bears accident and price drop cannot be called צאן ברזל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to אביי: If the owner took on accident and price drop, would you still call it צאן ברזל?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks אביי's answer from the previous step. He says the case אביי described is not even צאן ברזל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole meaning of צאן ברזל is that the owner's value is 'iron', guaranteed no matter what happens. If the owner takes on the losses from accidents and price drops, his money is not guaranteed anymore. So אביי's explanation does not fit the words of the משנה in בכורות, which calls it צאן ברזל.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'iron sheep'. The owner's value is guaranteed, as solid as iron.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' is אביי, whose answer we just learned.

phrases.english: If the owner accepted upon himself
accident and price drop,
would you call it צאן ברזל?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: אִי דְּקַבֵּיל עֲלֵיהּ מָרַהּ אוּנְסָא וְזוֹלָא
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that in בכורות the owner took on accident and price drop.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: צאן ברזל means the owner is guaranteed. If he bears the losses, the term no longer fits, yet the משנה in בכורות uses it.

steps.title: Our משנה should have made that distinction itself
steps.stepSummary: רבא's second challenge: if risk-bearing were the key, the משנה would have permitted the Jewish case when the owner carries the risk, instead of switching to גוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And also: instead of the last part saying 'But one may take צאן ברזל from גוים,' it should have made the distinction within the same case. It should have said: When is it forbidden? When the owner did not take on accident and price drop. But if the owner did take them on, it is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a second problem with אביי's answer. This time it comes from how our own משנה is worded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If an arrangement where the owner carries the risk were permitted and still called צאן ברזל, the משנה had an easy way to teach it. It could have split the Jewish case into forbidden and permitted versions. Instead it jumped to a different case, taking from גוים, which suggests אביי's distinction is not real.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore. It brings an additional challenge.
The last part of the משנה
Let it make the distinction within that same case
When is this said? It introduces a limit on a rule.
It is fine, it is allowed

phrases.english: And furthermore, instead of teaching in the last part:

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מְקַבְּלִין צֹאן בַּרְזֶל מִן הַגּוֹיִם
phrases.english: 'But one may take צאן ברזל from גוים,'
let it distinguish within that case itself:
When is this said?
When he did not accept accident and price drop upon himself;
but if the owner accepted accident and price drop,
it is fine!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, independent challenge to אביי's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's distinction between owner-bears-risk and owner-does-not-bear-risk.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that distinction existed, the משנה would naturally have taught it inside the Jewish case instead of moving to the case of גוים.

steps.title: רבא's answer: the גוי's claim exempts the offspring from בכורה
steps.stepSummary: In both cases the owner does not bear the risk, so the receiver owns the animals. The offspring are exempt from בכורה only because the גוי can seize them if he is not paid. This is called יד גוי באמצע, and any such animal is exempt from בכורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: In both cases the owner did not take on accident and price drop. The reason the offspring in בכורות are exempt from בכורה is this: if the receiver does not pay, the גוי comes and seizes the animal. If he cannot find the animal, he seizes the offspring. So a גוי's hand is in the middle, and any animal with a גוי's hand in the middle is exempt from בכורה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא drops אביי's approach and gives his own answer to the contradiction from step 4. Both משניות are about the same kind of deal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The receiver really owns the animals in both cases, which is why our משנה calls it רבית. The offspring are exempt from בכורה for a different reason: the גוי has a claim on them, since he can collect his debt from them. Even a partial claim by a גוי, without full ownership, is enough to exempt an animal from בכורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this and that, meaning both cases
Exempt from the laws of a firstborn animal
A גוי's hand is in the middle, meaning a גוי has some claim on the animal

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, צאן ברזל from a גוי belongs to the receiver. The offspring are exempt from בכורה only because the גוי can seize them, so a גוי's hand is in the middle.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the גוי owns the animals. The receiver owns them. The גוי only has a claim to collect from them, and that alone is enough for the בכורה exemption.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that ownership and a creditor's claim are separate. The animal can be the Jew's for the laws of רבית while still being exempt from בכורה because of the גוי's claim.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
Both this case and that case

phrases.aramaic: דְּלָא קַבֵּיל עֲלֵיהּ מָרַהּ אוּנְסָא וְזוֹלָא,
phrases.english: are where the owner did not accept accident and price drop upon himself.
And regarding the case in בכורות, this is the reason
that the offspring are exempt from בכורה:
since if he does not give the money,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the Jew who received the animals and owes the גוי.

phrases.english: the גוי comes and seizes the animal.
And if he does not find the animal,
he seizes the offspring,
and so there is a גוי's hand in the middle.
phrases.notes: 'In the middle' means the גוי has a share or claim on the animal, even though it is not fully his.

phrases.english: And any case where a גוי's hand is in the middle
is exempt from בכורה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting אביי's answer in steps 6 and 7, רבא gives a new resolution to the contradiction raised in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different reason (טעמא אחרינא): both cases are the same deal, and the בכורה exemption comes from a separate factor.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The בכורה exemption seemed to prove the animals still belong to the גוי, which would contradict our משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The receiver owns the animals in both cases. The offspring are exempt only because the גוי's right to seize them puts a גוי's hand in the middle, and any such animal is exempt from בכורה.

steps.title: What does 'him who has pity on the poor' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a פסוק in משלי about a person who grows rich through interest, and asks who the 'one who has pity on the poor' is.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'He who increases his wealth through interest and increase gathers it for the one who has pity on the poor.' Who is meant by 'the one who has pity on the poor'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new, aggadic section about interest. It quotes a פסוק and asks what one phrase in it means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the lender's money will end up with someone who is kind to the poor. The question is how that happens and who that person is. The answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: One who has pity on the poor

phrases.english: "He who increases his wealth through interest and increase
gathers it for the one who has pity on the poor."
What is meant by "the one who has pity on the poor"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new aggadic section, linked to the earlier discussion only because both deal with interest.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who is the 'one who has pity on the poor' who ends up with the lender's money?

steps.title: רב: someone like שבור מלכא
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that the money ends up with a ruler like שבור מלכא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: Someone like שבור מלכא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question. The 'one who has pity on the poor' is a king like שבור מלכא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lender will not keep his interest money. In the end it reaches the king, and the king is the one who looks after the poor.

phrases.english: Rav said:
Someone like King Shapur.
phrases.notes: The idea is that the interest money ends up in the king's hands.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The one who gathers the money is a ruler such as שבור מלכא.

steps.title: The verse applies even to interest from a gentile
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting הונא, says the פסוק is needed to teach that even interest taken from a גוי will not stay with the lender.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: הונא told me: The פסוק is needed only to teach that this applies even to interest from a גוי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן reports a teaching from הונא. The warning of the פסוק covers even interest that a Jew takes from a גוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone knows that interest from a fellow Jew is forbidden. הונא says the פסוק's special point is the גוי case: even that money will slip away from the lender. This sounds like he holds that taking interest from a גוי is a problem, and that sets up רבא's challenge.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן, אָמַר לִי הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said: Huna told me:
The verse is needed only
to teach that even interest from a gentile is included.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר לִי הוּנָא לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new point about the same פסוק: it includes interest from a גוי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The warning of 'מרבה הונו בנשך' applies even to interest taken from a גוי.

steps.title: רבא: the Torah permits taking interest from a gentile
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רב נחמן from the פסוק 'לנכרי תשיך', which seems to allow taking interest from a גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא challenged רב נחמן: 'To a גוי תשיך.' What does תשיך mean? Doesn't it mean 'take interest'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב נחמן's teaching. He brings a פסוק in דברים that seems to say you may take interest from a גוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the Torah allows taking interest from a גוי, why would a פסוק in משלי warn against it? רבא reads תשיך as תשוך, 'you may take interest'.

keyTerms.meaning: To a gentile you may lend with interest

phrases.english: Rava challenged Rav Naḥman:
"To a gentile tashikh"
What does tashikh mean? Doesn't it mean "take interest"?

steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim that the warning of משלי covers interest from a גוי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Torah says 'לנכרי תשיך', which seems to permit taking interest from a גוי, so it should not be condemned.

steps.title: תשיך means paying interest, not taking it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that תשיך means you may let the גוי take interest from you, meaning you may pay him interest.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means תשיך: you may pay him interest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב נחמן. The פסוק does not permit taking interest from a גוי. It permits paying interest to a גוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word is read as 'cause the גוי to take interest from you'. So the פסוק says nothing in favor of taking interest from a גוי, and רב נחמן's teaching stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him take interest from you, meaning pay interest

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two readings. רבא read the word as 'you take interest'. The answer reads it as 'you pay interest' to the גוי.

phrases.english: No, it means tashikh: pay interest.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the word of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: תשיך means you may take interest from a גוי.
steps.terutzMaskana: תשיך means you may pay interest to a גוי.

steps.title: Is paying interest to a gentile a requirement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the פסוק could really mean you must pay interest to a גוי, with no way around it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it not possible to do without this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new reading. The פסוק sounds like a command, and it makes no sense that the Torah would require us to pay interest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If תשיך means 'pay interest', the פסוק seems to order a Jew to borrow from a גוי with interest. Surely one can simply avoid borrowing. So what is the פסוק teaching?

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not enough; is it not possible

phrases.english: Is it not possible without this?
phrases.notes: He means: could the Torah really be commanding us to pay interest to a gentile?

steps.kashyaTarget: Reading תשיך as a command to pay interest to a גוי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There cannot be a מצוה to borrow with interest, so the פסוק cannot be a command to pay interest.

steps.title: The verse comes to exclude your brother
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק is not a command. It mentions the גוי only to teach that you may not pay interest to a fellow Jew.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to exclude your brother: to him you may not pay interest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק is not ordering anyone to pay interest. Its point is the contrast: to a גוי you may, to a fellow Jew you may not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'to a גוי' teach by implication that it is not allowed to a Jew. So the פסוק sets a limit rather than giving an obligation.

keyTerms.meaning: Your brother, meaning a fellow Jew

phrases.english: To exclude your brother, to whom you may not.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the פסוק as an exclusion, not a command
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק commands paying interest to a גוי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק mentions the גוי only to exclude a fellow Jew.

steps.title: Your brother is already stated explicitly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the same פסוק already says outright that you may not pay interest to your brother.
steps.simpleTranslation: About your brother it is written explicitly: 'And to your brother you shall not lend with interest!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last answer. Why learn about your brother by implication when the פסוק says it openly?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The end of the פסוק already forbids interest with a fellow Jew. So the words 'to a גוי' seem to add nothing, and the exclusion reading looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: And to your brother you shall not lend with interest

phrases.english: About your brother it is written explicitly:
"And to your brother you shall not lend with interest!"
phrases.notes: This is the second half of the same פסוק, דברים 23:21.

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'לנכרי' is needed to exclude a fellow Jew.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The exclusion is already stated explicitly in the same פסוק, so it would be extra.

steps.title: Both a positive and a negative command
steps.stepSummary: The extra wording teaches that paying interest to a Jew breaks both an עשה and a לא תעשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is to make him transgress both a positive command and a negative command.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the extra words are not wasted. Someone who pays interest to a fellow Jew breaks two מצוות, not one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'To a גוי you may pay interest' implies 'only to a גוי', and that counts as an עשה. 'To your brother you shall not' is a לא תעשה. So paying interest to a Jew breaks both.
steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק 'לנכרי תשיך' is read as 'you may pay interest to a גוי', not 'take interest'. That keeps רב נחמן's teaching standing. Paying interest to a fellow Jew breaks both an עשה and a לא תעשה.

phrases.english: To make him transgress
both a positive command and a negative command.
phrases.notes: The positive command comes from 'to a gentile,' which implies 'only to a gentile.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16 and closes רבא's first objection. A second objection to רב נחמן follows in step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the extra words add another מצוה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The exclusion of 'your brother' is extra, since it is stated explicitly.
steps.terutzMaskana: The implied exclusion adds an עשה on top of the explicit לא תעשה.

steps.title: The משנה seems to allow lending to a גוי with interest
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רב נחמן from our משנה, which allows both borrowing from and lending to a גוי with interest, and the same for a גר תושב.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him: The משנה says, 'One may borrow from them and lend to them with interest, and the same is true for a גר תושב!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes our own משנה to challenge the view of רב נחמן that a Jew should not lend to a גוי with interest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists both borrowing and lending with interest as allowed with a גוי. That sounds like it is fully allowed from the start. This clashes with the ruling that lending to a גוי with interest is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jew who accepted the seven מצוות of בני נח and lives in the land of ישראל, but did not fully convert

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think this challenge is about borrowing from a גוי. Paying interest to a גוי was already shown to be allowed. The problem is the word 'מלוין', lending to him with interest.

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
phrases.notes: רבא is challenging רב נחמן here, using our משנה.

phrases.english: One may borrow from them and lend to them with interest,
and the same is true of a גר תושב!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first objection from the פסוק was answered (steps 12-17), רבא raises a second objection against רב נחמן's teaching in step 11, this time from our משנה (step 2).
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling of רב נחמן that one may not lend to a גוי with interest
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה plainly says 'ומלוין אותם ברבית', which means lending to a גוי with interest is allowed. That contradicts a ban on it.

steps.title: The משנה's permission applies only to a narrow case
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בריה דרב הונא begins to answer that the משנה's ruling is needed only for a limited situation. The rest of his answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא, the son of רב הונא, said: This ruling is needed only...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer by limiting the משנה to a specific case. This line is a setup, and the actual case he means comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'לא נצרכה אלא' means 'this was only needed for...'. It narrows the משנה so that it does not give full permission. That way the משנה no longer clashes with the ruling against lending to a גוי with interest.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed only for... It narrows a source to a specific case.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Chiyya, son of Rav Huna, said:
It is needed only…
phrases.notes: He is talking about the משנה's permission to lend with interest. The sentence finishes on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the משנה in step 18 by narrowing its scope.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source to a specific case (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to allow lending to any גוי with interest, freely and from the start.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה's permission is needed only for a narrow situation, which is spelled out in the continuation.
